subject: NorthBay continuity evidence: RTO/RPO clarifications
messages:
From: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@northbay.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@northbay.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: continuity evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor review for NorthBay’s Platform Risk Committee we need a concise package covering your business continuity and disaster recovery posture. Specific asks:

- The most recent RTO and RPO test results (what was tested, duration to recovery, recovery point achieved).
- Runbook describing failover steps for the inference API and the embedding store (high-level is fine).
- Backup retention and restore validation for customer data (where snapshots live and how long).
- Date of last full DR exercise and any outstanding action items.

Can you send the artifacts or point us to a shared drive? We may need a short attestation on company letterhead depending on the committee outcome.

Thanks,
Patricia Gomez
Sr. Vendor Risk Analyst
NorthBay Financial
patricia.gomez@northbay.com

Subject: Re: Request: continuity evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

Hi Patricia — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a short packet and a few logs that should directly address the committee’s questions. Highlights up front:

- Most recent DR table-top + partial failover: 2026-04-16. Full functional failover of inference control plane (stateless frontends + model-serving replicas) completed in 37 minutes; RTO target for control plane = 60 minutes.
- RPO: for customer data in cold backups = 24 hours; for live embedding store (hot) we maintain continuous replication to a standby region with measured RPO < 5 minutes during normal ops.
- Attached: redwood_bcp_summary_2026-05.pdf (2-page exec summary), rto_rpo_testlog_q1-2026.csv (test matrix + timings), runbook_v3.md (operational failover runbook excerpt).

We map these controls to SOC 2 CC7 and to SIG-Lite items; see the summary page for the mapping table. We also have a recorded DR runbook walkthrough (link below) and are planning a fuller recovery drill (live failover) on 2026-06-10 — happy to invite a NorthBay observer.

If the committee wants a signed attestation, please indicate the exact language and we’ll route to legal.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Olga — thanks for the fast turnaround and the packet. A couple of clarifying questions from the committee before we circulate:

1) The summary notes RPO < 5 minutes for the embedding store under normal ops. Can you clarify whether that applies to the entire embeddings dataset or just active shards? We need to understand scope to assess potential data loss for historical embeddings.

2) The runbook mentions KV cache warm-up and prefix caching — can you confirm the expected cold-start latency if cache priming is required during failover? The committee expects a short note with measured numbers.

3) For backups: can you include the S3 lifecycle policy or retention snapshot that shows the 365-day retention noted in the summary?

If you can add short attachments addressing 1–3 that would be ideal. Would you also be able to provide a one-paragraph attestation on company letterhead confirming the test date and outcome?

Appreciate it,
Patricia

Subject: Re: Request: continuity evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

Hi Patricia — following up with the clarifications you requested and the supplemental artifacts. Apologies for the short delay; we wanted to validate numbers against the April drill logs.

Answers to your numbered items:
1) Embedding store RPO scope: our continuous replication is applied at shard-level for the entire embeddings dataset (all active and historical shards). During normal operations replication lag is typically < 5 minutes; in the April run the maximum observed lag was 3 minutes and 42 seconds. See attached kv-cache-persistence-note.txt for shard/replica notes.

2) KV cache and prefix caching: when the standby region becomes active we rely on prefix caching + on-demand warm-up. Measured cold-start impact from the April partial failover: median 95th-percentile latency increased by ~14s for cold keys; roughly ~8% of requests were served without cache for the first 25 minutes. Neha included the validated stats.

3) Backups: attached is the S3 lifecycle excerpt showing the 365-day retention and current object counts for the backup prefix (bucket: redwood-customer-backups-prod). We also included a short CSV of the RTO/RPO test matrix.

Attached: s3_backup_lifecycle_policy.txt (policy excerpt), kv-cache-persistence-note.txt (short note + measured numbers), rto_rpo_testlog_q1-2026.csv (previously sent).

We can provide a signed attestation — Monica has a draft and Legal is ready to sign once you confirm the exact wording you need. Also, if useful, we can schedule a 20-minute walkthrough before your committee meeting; propose 2026-06-04 or 2026-06-08 (PST).

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Trust & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
